title: How to reset canva desktop app on mac in 10 minutes, without losing designs
metaTitle: How to reset Canva desktop app on Mac, step by step
description: How to reset Canva desktop app on Mac: quit Canva, clear its Library folders, then relaunch. Save unsaved work first, and keep the app itself.
targetKeyword: how to reset canva desktop app on mac
secondaryKeywords: canva desktop app not working mac
intro: To reset the Canva desktop app on Mac, quit Canva with ⌘Q, move its leftover Library files to the Trash, then open Canva again. Your designs live in your Canva account, so a reset clears local app data, but save any unsaved work first.
tldr: Test Canva in a browser, then update the app and macOS before you reset.
Quit Canva with ⌘Q, then trash the Canva items in ~/Library and keep the app itself.
Save unsaved work first. Canva says no designs are lost in a reset.
Canva's own help pages could not be opened during our research, so the Library method comes from third-party tests.

blocks.text: What a reset actually clears

A reset clears the local files Canva keeps on your Mac. Those files include settings, cached pages and logs. Your designs live with your Canva account, not only on this Mac. That is why a reset is safer than most people expect. Still, save everything before you delete a single file.

The desktop app runs the same design features as Canva in a browser. It adds tabs, pop-out windows, system notifications, Memory Saver and the ability to open supported files from Finder or the Dock, according to lilachbullock.com. It adds no design features of its own. So if the browser version works, the fault sits in the desktop app.
Try the easy fixes before a reset

A reset takes longer than an update, so run the cheap checks first. A third-party guide lists the order as: test in a browser, update the app, update macOS, reset the app, and force quit only as a last resort. Follow that order and you may skip the reset altogether.

items: Test canva.com in Safari or Chrome.
Update the Canva desktop app from Update App in the top corner.
Update macOS from System Settings > General > Software Update.
Reset the app by moving its Library files to the Trash.
Force quit only as a last resort, because it can lose unsaved changes.

blocks.text: The update step matters more than it looks. Canva's download page offers one universal build for Macs with Intel or Apple chips. The newest build we found was 1.126.0. Mole's test saw 1.125.1 update to 1.126.0 on its own. If your build is older, updating may fix the problem without any reset.
Find the Canva files in your Library folder

The Library folder is hidden in Finder by default. You can open it without unhiding anything. Use Go > Go to Folder, type ~/Library, and press Return. The Canva items sit in a few places, and the table below lists them.

rows: The main folder for the reset
Temporary files the app can recreate
Safe to trash after you save your work
Keep a copy if you want to report a problem later
Preferences and Saved Application State files
Match names that include Canva or com.canva
Background items that start at login
Check the name before you trash it

blocks.title: Save before you trash anything
blocks.text: Upload unsaved work first. Mole's write-up, citing Canva's help, says deleting these folders does not lose designs as long as unsaved work is uploaded first.

Keep the Canva app itself in Applications. The reset works on the data around the app. If you also trash Canva.app, you have moved from a reset to a full uninstall, which is a bigger step and creates more work.
Relaunch and confirm the reset worked

Open Canva from Applications and sign in if asked. Check that your recent designs appear. Open one design, make a small change, and wait for it to save. If the window looks too large or too small, go to View > Interface scale > Reset to Default.

Test tabs and pop-out windows too, since those are desktop-only features. If a tab fails to load, close it and reopen the design. Mole's notes say removing the app does not cancel a Canva Pro or Teams subscription.
The Help menu reset you may see

Some guides mention a built-in reset under Help > Troubleshooting > Reset App Data. The only source we found is a 2024 Canva Support reply on X. We could not open that post, and Canva's own help pages could not be opened during our research. So we cannot confirm that menu item in your version. Look for it, but don't rely on it. The Library method works without it.

blocks.title: Unconfirmed menu path
blocks.text: If Reset App Data is in your Help menu, it may do the same job as the folder method. Check the result the same way: relaunch Canva and test a design.

A June 2024 Apple Community thread, about Canva 1.87.0 on macOS Sonoma 14.5, suggests Canva > Preferences > Advanced > Clear Cache. Canva has not confirmed that path. Use it only if you cannot find a reset menu and the folder method did not help.
When the browser fails too

If canva.com fails in a browser, a desktop reset will not help. Techsifted's 2026 troubleshooting guide suggests a hard refresh, clearing only canva.com site data in Chrome, and testing in an Incognito window. Check the status page early, because an outage on Canva's side needs no fix from you.

items: Check status.canva.com first. If it shows a problem, wait for Canva to fix it.
Hard refresh the page with ⇧⌘R in Chrome.
In Chrome, open Settings > Privacy > Site data and remove only canva.com.
Test in an Incognito window to see whether your browser data is the cause.
For failed exports, try PNG instead of PDF, or export a shorter section.

blocks.text: Common mistakes people make
The most common mistake is trashing the whole app when only the Library data is broken. That turns a reset into a reinstall. Reinstall only if the app will not open after the reset and update.
The second mistake is force quitting before saving. Force quit can lose unsaved changes, so save first and use it last.

The third mistake is leaving the login item behind. Mole found that Canva's login item can stay listed after the app is trashed. Turn it off in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions, or Canva may open at every login.
The fourth mistake is trashing random files. Only remove items whose names mention Canva. Other files in your Library may belong to other apps or to macOS itself.
Version checks and old app versions

Canva may disable desktop app versions older than six months, or at any time after a critical bug or vulnerability is identified, according to lilachbullock.com. If your build is old, updating matters more than resetting. Check Update App before you touch the Library folder.

The newest build we found is 1.126.0. Third-party sites date it 2026-09-18, so Canva may have shipped a newer build since then. Canva's download page does not list a version number, so Update App is the most reliable check.
Reinstall or uninstall when a reset is not enough

If the app still fails, remove it and install it again. Mole's notes list two Homebrew commands for this. The command brew uninstall --cask --zap canva removes the app and its data. The command brew uninstall --cask canva removes only the app.
Download the app again from Canva's download page for Mac, then sign in with your Canva account. Your designs load from your account, so you do not need to rebuild them.
Where to go next

If you use Canva for client work, the [Canva for designers page](/for/designers/canva) covers resizing, brand kits and exports on Mac. Keep the update and browser checks in mind, because they solve most of the problems people report.

faq.question: Will resetting the Canva desktop app delete my designs?
faq.answer: Canva says no designs are lost in a reset, according to lilachbullock.com, which cites Canva's help. Mole adds one condition: upload any unsaved work first. Designs you saved to your Canva account stay there.

faq.question: Is a reset the same as uninstalling Canva?
faq.answer: No. A reset removes local data and keeps the app in Applications. An uninstall also moves Canva.app to the Trash. Mole's notes say removing the app does not cancel a Canva Pro or Teams subscription.

faq.question: Where is the Reset App Data option in Canva?
faq.answer: Some sources point to Help > Troubleshooting > Reset App Data. The only source we found is a 2024 Canva Support reply on X, which we could not open. Check your Help menu. If the item is missing, use the Library method in this guide.

faq.question: Do I need to reinstall Canva after a reset?
faq.answer: Usually not. The Library method keeps the app. Reinstall only when the app will not open after a reset and an update.

faq.question: Why does Canva ask me to update the Mac app?
faq.answer: Canva may disable desktop app versions older than six months, or at any time after a critical bug or vulnerability is identified, according to lilachbullock.com. Update App in the top corner handles the update.

faq.question: What is the latest Canva version for Mac?
faq.answer: The newest build we found is 1.126.0, listed by third-party sites with a release date of 2026-09-18. Canva's download page does not list a version, so check Update App for the build you have.

faq.question: Does a reset fix a blank or white screen?
faq.answer: It can, if damaged local data is the cause. First test canva.com in a browser and check status.canva.com. If the browser also fails, the reset will not help. Forum threads report similar fixes, but Canva has not confirmed them.

faq.question: Can I reset only the browser version of Canva?
faq.answer: Yes. In Chrome, open Settings > Privacy > Site data and remove only canva.com. That does not touch the desktop app's Library folders, so the two fixes stay separate.

task: Reset the Canva desktop app on Mac
appliesTo: Canva desktop app for Mac, Apple silicon and Intel, macOS Sonoma and later
requirements: A Mac with an Apple chip or an Intel processor, the two types Canva's download page lists
A Canva account with your designs saved to Canva
Your Mac password, if macOS asks for it during updates
Access to Finder, so you can open your Library folder

steps.name: Test Canva in a browser
steps.text: Open canva.com in Safari or Chrome and sign in. If your designs load and edit normally there, the problem is in the desktop app, and a reset is worth trying.
steps.tip: The browser test takes less time than a reset and shows where the fault sits.

steps.name: Update the Canva desktop app
steps.text: In the Canva desktop app, click Update App in the top corner. In the dialog, click Update Canva App, then wait while the app closes and relaunches.
steps.tip: If the update button is missing, you may already be on the newest build.

steps.name: Update macOS
steps.text: Open System Settings, go to General, then Software Update. Install any pending macOS update, restart if asked, and test Canva again.
steps.tip: On Sonoma and later the menu is System Settings. Older guides still say System Preferences.

steps.name: Quit Canva completely
steps.text: Click Canva in the menu bar, then choose Quit Canva. You can also press ⌘Q while Canva is the front app. Wait until the Canva icon leaves the Dock.

steps.name: Force quit only if Canva will not close
steps.text: If Canva will not quit, choose Apple menu > Force Quit, select Canva, then click Force Quit. Force quitting can lose unsaved changes, so use it only as a last resort.
steps.tip: Save any open design first, if you can, before you force quit.

steps.name: Confirm Canva has fully exited
steps.text: Open Activity Monitor from Applications > Utilities. Search for Canva in the search box. Make sure no Canva processes are still running before you continue.
steps.tip: A leftover Canva helper process can lock files you are trying to move.

steps.name: Make sure your work is saved
steps.text: Open each design you need and confirm it has finished saving to Canva. Mole's write-up, citing Canva's help, says designs are safe when unsaved work is uploaded first.

steps.name: Open your Library folder in Finder
steps.text: Click the Finder icon in the Dock. Choose Go > Go to Folder, type ~/Library, then press Return. Finder opens your Library folder without you unhiding it.
steps.tip: The Library folder is hidden by default. Typing the path avoids needing to unhide it.

steps.name: Trash the Canva Application Support folder
steps.text: Open Application Support inside Library and find the Canva folder at ~/Library/Application Support/Canva. Drag it to the Trash. Keep the Canva app in Applications.

steps.name: Trash the Canva cache and logs
steps.text: Move ~/Library/Caches/com.canva.CanvaDesktop and ~/Library/Logs/Canva to the Trash. Caches hold temporary files, and logs hold records of recent errors.

steps.name: Trash Canva preferences, saved state and the LaunchAgents plist
steps.text: Look for Canva files in ~/Library/Preferences and ~/Library/Saved Application State. Then look for a Canva plist in ~/Library/LaunchAgents. Trash only files whose names mention Canva or com.canva.
steps.tip: Mole's list names these places but not every exact file name. Check each name before you trash it.

steps.name: Empty the Trash
steps.text: Choose File > Empty Trash in Finder, then confirm. This removes the files you just moved, so only do it after you have checked the names.

steps.name: Open Canva again
steps.text: Open Canva from Applications. Sign in if asked, and check that your recent designs appear. If the app still misbehaves, restart your Mac and open Canva once more.

steps.name: Reset the interface size if the layout looks wrong
steps.text: In Canva, choose View > Interface scale > Reset to Default. This fixes text and panels that look too big or too small after the reset.

troubleshooting.fix: Use Apple menu > Force Quit, then open Activity Monitor and confirm no Canva processes remain. Save first if you can, because force quit can lose unsaved changes.

troubleshooting.problem: Canva still fails after the reset
troubleshooting.fix: Test canva.com in a browser to see whether the problem is the app or your account. Then check status.canva.com for an outage on Canva's side.

troubleshooting.problem: Canva asks you to update or says the version is too old
troubleshooting.fix: Click Update App in the top corner and follow the prompts. Canva may disable desktop versions older than six months, according to a third-party guide.

troubleshooting.problem: Canva starts at login after you trash it
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off the login item in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions. Mole found it can stay listed after the app is trashed.

troubleshooting.problem: A 2024 forum reply suggests clearing the cache in Preferences
troubleshooting.fix: The path Canva > Preferences > Advanced > Clear Cache came from a community reply, and Canva has not confirmed it. Use it only if the folder method does not help.

troubleshooting.problem: Designs look blank or exports fail in the browser
troubleshooting.fix: Hard refresh with ⇧⌘R in Chrome, remove only canva.com site data under Settings > Privacy > Site data, and try PNG instead of PDF for exports.
